The body reached the guest (`< /tmp/radarr_client.json` into `pct exec … -d @-`, an outer-shell redirection) and every heredoc imported what it used, so §17.1377 let it through. It exited 22 on its own test call, and the machines were then read: the top-level `username`/`password` it set came back ABSENT and `fields.password` held the literal asterisks the GET had masked it with. Secrets by NAME only.

#!/bin/bash
set -e

# --- 1. qBittorrent: set WebUI username/password (idempotent — skip if login already works) ---
if ! curl -s -d "username=admin&password=$MASS_PASSWORD" http://192.168.1.24:8080/api/v2/auth/login | grep -q '^Ok\.$'; then
    pct exec 105 -- systemctl stop qbittorrent-nox.service
    HASH=$(python3 - <<'EOF'
import base64, hashlib, os
salt = os.urandom(16)
key = hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac('sha512', os.environ['MASS_PASSWORD'].encode(), salt, 100000, 64)
print('@ByteArray(' + base64.b64encode(salt).decode() + ':' + base64.b64encode(key).decode() + ')')
EOF
)
    pct exec 105 -- sh -c "sed -i '/^\[Preferences\]/a WebUI\\\\Username=admin\nWebUI\\\\Password_PBKDF2=$HASH' /var/lib/qbittorrent-nox/.config/qBittorrent/qBittorrent.conf"
    pct exec 105 -- systemctl start qbittorrent-nox.service
    sleep 2
    if ! curl -s -d "username=admin&password=$MASS_PASSWORD" http://192.168.1.24:8080/api/v2/auth/login | grep -q '^Ok\.$'; then
        echo "ERROR: qBittorrent login failed after setting password" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
fi
echo "qBittorrent login: Ok."

# --- 2. Radarr: update download client with priority=1 and credentials ---
RADARR_KEY=$(pct exec 103 -- sh -c 'sed -n "s:.*<ApiKey>\(.*\)</ApiKey>.*:\1:p" /var/lib/radarr/config.xml | head -n 1')
RADARR_CLIENT=$(pct exec 103 -- sh -c "curl -s -H 'X-Api-Key: $RADARR_KEY' http://127.0.0.1:7878/api/v3/downloadclient")
RADARR_ID=$(echo "$RADARR_CLIENT" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)[0]["id"])')
echo "$RADARR_CLIENT" | python3 -c '
import json, sys
clients = json.load(sys.stdin)
c = clients[0]
c["priority"] = 1
c["username"] = "admin"
c["password"] = "'"$MASS_PASSWORD"'"
print(json.dumps(c))
' > /tmp/radarr_client.json
pct exec 103 -- sh -c "curl -s --fail-with-body -X PUT -H 'X-Api-Key: $RADARR_KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @- http://127.0.0.1:7878/api/v3/downloadclient/$RADARR_ID" < /tmp/radarr_client.json

# --- 3. Sonarr: update download client with priority=1 and credentials ---
SONARR_KEY=$(pct exec 104 -- sh -c 'sed -n "s:.*<ApiKey>\(.*\)</ApiKey>.*:\1:p" /var/lib/sonarr/config.xml | head -n 1')
SONARR_CLIENT=$(pct exec 104 -- sh -c "curl -s -H 'X-Api-Key: $SONARR_KEY' http://127.0.0.1:8989/api/v3/downloadclient")
SONARR_ID=$(echo "$SONARR_CLIENT" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)[0]["id"])')
echo "$SONARR_CLIENT" | python3 -c '
import json, sys
clients = json.load(sys.stdin)
c = clients[0]
c["priority"] = 1
c["username"] = "admin"
c["password"] = "'"$MASS_PASSWORD"'"
print(json.dumps(c))
' > /tmp/sonarr_client.json
pct exec 104 -- sh -c "curl -s --fail-with-body -X PUT -H 'X-Api-Key: $SONARR_KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @- http://127.0.0.1:8989/api/v3/downloadclient/$SONARR_ID" < /tmp/sonarr_client.json

# --- 4. Test both connections ---
echo "--- Radarr test ---"
pct exec 103 -- sh -c "curl -s --fail-with-body -X POST -H 'X-Api-Key: $RADARR_KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' http://127.0.0.1:7878/api/v3/downloadclient/test"
echo ""
echo "--- Sonarr test ---"
pct exec 104 -- sh -c "curl -s --fail-with-body -X POST -H 'X-Api-Key: $SONARR_KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' http://127.0.0.1:8989/api/v3/downloadclient/test"
echo ""
